mechanism: Added lz::BinaryTreeMatchFinder: insertion keeps each hash bucket as a binary search tree ordered by the candidate's suffix bytes (LZMA bt4 shape), so one downward walk both inserts the new position and returns the longest match among the nodes on the insertion path, instead of MatchFinder's hash chain walking candidates newest-first up to a fixed max_tries. With max_depth at least the bucket's tree height the match is length-exact, proven equal to a brute-force scan of the same hash bucket. Does not yet carry WINDOW eviction (the tree only grows) or the len0/len1 prefix-reuse optimization real bt4 finders use (comparisons always start from scratch via a new suffix_common_len helper) -- both are speed/memory work left for the wiring slice. Factored MatchFinder's prefix hash into a shared prefix_hash function so the two finders' hash-bucket notion cannot drift apart. 6 unit tests: no match before any insertion; an exact repeat's length/distance checked directly; a brute-force cross-check over 400 bytes of low-entropy pseudo-random data (Xorshift32 mod 5) confirming exactness when max_depth cannot truncate the walk; zero max_depth finds nothing but leaves the tree consistent; a 65,000+-byte identical run stays within MAX_MATCH_LEN without hanging. All five root CLAUDE.md gates clean (one private-intra-doc-link warning from the public struct's docs naming private MatchFinder/suffix_common_len, fixed by dropping the links).
